cases.sentence: Я повернул за ___ и постучался в первую же дверь.
options: угол
угла
углу
углом
cases.explain: «За» meaning motion round or behind something takes the accusative; угол is inanimate, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

options: душа
души
душе
душой
cases.explain: Absence expressed with «ни единой» puts the missing thing in the genitive, exactly as «нет» would.

options: рай
рая
раю
раем
cases.explain: «Нет» in the sense 'there is none' always governs the genitive, so рай becomes рая.

options: мир
мира
миру
миром
cases.explain: The person or thing laughed at with «смеяться в глаза» is the indirect object and stands in the dative: этому миру.

options: мир
мира
миру
мире
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (location, not direction) requires the prepositional: в этом мире.

cases.sentence: Царица не пришла к тебе на перрон, с ___, опущенными ниц.
options: ресницы
ресниц
ресницам
ресницами
cases.explain: «С» meaning 'with, having' governs the instrumental, here in the plural: с ресницами.

options: время
времени
временем
времена
cases.explain: In the «зачем тебе …?» construction the thing you supposedly need is the subject of an unspoken 'is', so it stays in the nominative.

reading.question: Why does the voice say it makes no difference whether Venichka turns left or right?
options: Because he has nowhere to go anyway
Because both roads lead back to the station
Because the shops are still shut
Because he has no money left
reading.correct: Because he has nowhere to go anyway
reading.explain: The voice tells him he may as well walk straight ahead, since he has nowhere to go in any case.

reading.question: What is Venichka considering trying?
options: Breathing deeply forty times over, which he was told makes a person die
Knocking at the first door on the square
Asking a passer-by for the time
Walking back to the platform to wait
reading.correct: Breathing deeply forty times over, which he was told makes a person die
reading.explain: Someone once told him that forty deep breaths in and out would make a person give up the ghost, and he wonders whether to try it.

reading.ru: Да ведь у кого узнать, если на площади ни единой души, то есть решительно ни единой?..
reading.question: Why can Venichka not find out what time it is?
options: There is not a single soul on the square to ask
The station clock has stopped
He is too drunk to read a clock
Nobody will answer a stranger at night
reading.correct: There is not a single soul on the square to ask
reading.explain: He asks himself whom he could possibly ask when the square is completely empty.

reading.ru: Мы все как бы пьяны, только каждый по-своему, один выпил больше, другой меньше.
reading.question: What does Venichka say about people in general?
options: That everyone is drunk in his own way, some having drunk more and some less
That everyone is sober except him
That nobody in the world has ever been drunk
That people drink only out of grief
reading.correct: That everyone is drunk in his own way, some having drunk more and some less
reading.explain: He compares human life to a brief squinting of the soul and says we are all drunk, each in his own way.

reading.ru: Одного уже вытошнило, и ему хорошо, а другого только еще начинает тошнить.
reading.question: How does Venichka describe the different stages people are at?
options: One has already been sick and feels fine, another is only starting to feel sick
One is asleep and another is awake
One is laughing and another is counting his money
One has gone home and another is still on the square
reading.correct: One has already been sick and feels fine, another is only starting to feel sick
reading.explain: It is part of his list of how the world's drunkenness takes different people differently.

reading.question: What does Venichka say he will do when the Lord asks him why he is silent?
options: Go on saying nothing at all
Tell Him the whole truth about his life
Ask Him what time it is
Laugh in reply
reading.correct: Go on saying nothing at all
reading.explain: He answers his own question by saying he will just keep silent, silent.

reading.question: Why does the inner voice say there is no longer any point in learning the time?
options: Because his heavenly paradise is gone and no one met him
Because the trains have all stopped running
Because he is about to fall asleep anyway
Because he already asked someone an hour ago
reading.correct: Because his heavenly paradise is gone and no one met him
reading.explain: The voice argues that he used to check the time when he still had a paradise to go to, and now he has none.

reading.ru: Утеха рода человеческого, лилия долины – не пришла и не встретила.
reading.question: What happened with the woman Venichka was expecting?
options: She neither came nor met him
She met him but did not speak
She met him on the wrong platform
She sent someone else in her place
reading.correct: She neither came nor met him
reading.explain: The consolation of mankind, the lily of the valley, simply did not come and did not meet him.

reading.ru: «Не женщина, а бланманже», как ты в шутку ее называл, – на перрон к тебе не пришла.
reading.question: What did Venichka jokingly call her?
options: Not a woman but a blancmange
Not a woman but a thunderstorm
Not a woman but a railway station
Not a woman but a song
reading.correct: Not a woman but a blancmange
reading.explain: The nickname he used in jest was «не женщина, а бланманже».

reading.ru: Я повернул за угол и постучался в первую же дверь.
reading.question: How does the chapter end?
options: He turns the corner and knocks at the very first door
He lies down on the empty square
He walks back into the station building
He finally meets a living soul
reading.correct: He turns the corner and knocks at the very first door
reading.explain: After being told to go and ask at any threshold in Petushki, he turns the corner and knocks at the first door he comes to.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that it makes no difference which way Venichka goes?
sentences: «Если хочешь идти налево, Веничка, – иди налево.
Если хочешь направо – иди направо.
Все равно тебе некуда идти.
Так что уж лучше иди вперед, куда глаза глядят…»
highlight.explain: The third sentence gives the reason — he has nowhere to go in any case.

highlight.question: Which sentence explains why there is nobody Venichka could ask the time from?
sentences: О, погоди, погоди!..
Может, время сначала узнать?
Узнать, сколько времени?..
Да ведь у кого узнать, если на площади ни единой души, то есть решительно ни единой?..
Да если б и встретилась живая душа – смог бы ты разве разомкнуть уста, от холода и от горя?
Да, от горя и от холода… О, немота!..
highlight.explain: The fourth sentence states that the square is completely empty, so there is no one to ask.

highlight.question: Which sentence gives the joking nickname Venichka used for her?
sentences: Да зачем тебе время, Веничка?
Лучше иди, иди, закройся от ветра и потихоньку иди…
Был у тебя когда-то небесный рай, узнавал бы время в прошлую пятницу – а теперь небесного рая больше нет, зачем тебе время?
Царица не пришла к тебе на перрон, с ресницами, опущенными ниц; божество от тебя отвернулось, – так зачем тебе узнавать время?
«Не женщина, а бланманже», как ты в шутку ее называл, – на перрон к тебе не пришла.
Утеха рода человеческого, лилия долины – не пришла и не встретила.
Какой же смысл после этого узнавать тебе время, Веничка?..
highlight.explain: Only the fifth sentence quotes the joking name he gave her.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells Venichka to go into a Petushki house and ask a question at the threshold?
sentences: Что тебе осталось? утром – стон, вечером – плач, ночью – скрежет зубовный…
И кому, кому в мире есть дело до твоего сердца?
Кому?..
Вот, войди в любой петушинский дом, у любого порога спроси: «Какое вам дело до моего сердца?»
Боже мой…
highlight.explain: The fourth sentence is the instruction to enter any house in Petushki and ask at the threshold.
